title: strychnos innocua var. burtonii
intro: Strychnos innocua var. burtonii, commonly known as the West African Strychnine Tree, is a plant species belonging to the Loganiaceae family. It has been traditionally used in African folk medicine for its various health benefits, including treating fever, rheumatism, and respiratory issues, as well as being used as an analgesic and anti-inflammatory agent. The therapeutic actions of Strychnos innocua var. burtonii are attributed to its bioactive constituents, which include alkaloids such as strychnine and other glycosides, flavonoids, and phenolic compounds. The plant's bioactive constituents are responsible for its analgesic, anti-inflammatory, and antipyretic properties, making it a valuable resource in traditional medicine.
